title: A Slow Provider Consumes the Whole Pool
description: A service accepts 500 requests/s. A dependency slows from 200 ms to 2 s, and the service has 200 concurrent slots. Which response addresses the resulting pressure?

options.text: Use an unbounded waiting queue so no caller sees rejection.
options.explanation: The deficit becomes rising latency and memory use; it does not disappear.

options.text: Retry every slow call at every layer.
options.explanation: Nested retries amplify load on the already-slow dependency.

options.text: Propagate deadlines, bound admission and isolate the dependency's pool.
options.explanation: Little's law gives about 100 in-flight calls normally and 1,000 at 2 s, beyond 200 slots. Limits and bulkheads protect the service; capacity or load must change to resolve a sustained deficit.

options.text: Remove timeouts so completed work is never interrupted.
options.explanation: Long waits retain scarce slots and allow one failing dependency to exhaust the service.
